summary.name: Multipass
summary.one_liner: Multipass is a Canonical tool for launching and managing Ubuntu virtual machines on Windows, macOS, and Linux with a single command.
use_cases: Launch throwaway Ubuntu VMs for testing
Simulate a cloud deployment on a workstation
Share files between host and Ubuntu VM
Try Kubernetes or OpenStack on a local Ubuntu instance
summary.what_it_does: Multipass launches and runs Ubuntu virtual machines from the command line and can initialise them with cloud-init metadata, similar to public cloud instances. It uses each platform's native hypervisor: Host Compute System on Windows, the Apple Virtualization framework on macOS, and QEMU on Linux. It automatically fetches the latest Ubuntu images from Canonical and offers cloud-tuned images. It also supports sharing files and folders between host and instances, and gives the 'primary' instance special filesystem integration and hot-key access.
notable: Uses native hypervisors: HCS on Windows, Apple Virtualization framework on macOS, QEMU on Linux
cloud-init support to configure VMs like public cloud instances
Growing catalogue of images with pre-installed applications
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page
Catalogue of pre-installed application images is still growing
